# Multi-Tenant Document Store REST API

## Resources

```
POST   /v1/documents                    # Create
GET    /v1/documents                    # List (paginated)
GET    /v1/documents/{id}               # Read
PUT    /v1/documents/{id}               # Update (creates version)
DELETE /v1/documents/{id}               # Soft delete
GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions      # List versions
GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions/{v}  # Read specific version
POST   /v1/documents/{id}/restore       # Restore from version
```

**Decisions:**
- Single `/documents` endpoint per tenant (tenant from header/JWT, not URL path). Cleaner than `/tenants/{t}/documents` and avoids coupling routing to multi-tenancy.
- Soft delete only (no `DELETE` hard-delete). Compliance + audit trail matter more than storage.
- Versions implicit on every `PUT`—no separate "create version" action. Simpler than explicit versioning endpoints.
- No search endpoint here (add `/v1/search` separately if needed; keep documents CRUD clean).

---

## Auth Model

**Bearer Token + Tenant Context:**

```
Authorization: Bearer {jwt}

JWT payload:
{
  "sub": "{user_id}",
  "tenant_id": "{tenant_id}",
  "scope": "documents:read documents:write",
  "exp": 1234567890
}
```

**Per-document permissions** (optional, in DB):
- Owner can grant read/write/admin to other users in same tenant.
- Query filters by tenant_id + user_id (or granted_to).

**Decisions:**
- JWT in Authorization header (standard, cacheable, no session storage).
- Tenant in JWT, not URL. Prevents routing mistakes, simplifies middleware.
- Scope string over role enum: more granular, scales to new actions.
- No API keys for now (add only if service-to-service calls needed). YAGNI.
- Permissions in DB optional: start with tenant-wide access (all users in tenant see all docs), add ACLs when asked.

---

## Pagination

```
GET /v1/documents?limit=20&offset=0

Response:
{
  "data": [...],
  "pagination": {
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 20,
    "total": 156,
    "has_next": true
  }
}
```

**Decisions:**
- Offset/limit over cursor: simpler, works for small datasets (most document stores). Switch to cursor if you hit 100k+ docs and offset becomes slow.
- `total` count in response: useful for UIs, cheap if you already have count in DB query.
- Max limit: 100 (enforce server-side, default 20). Prevents accidental full-table fetches.
- No sort: default by created_at DESC. Add `?sort=updated_at,name:asc` later if needed.

---

## Versioning

**Implicit, automatic:**
- Every `PUT` creates a new version automatically.
- `GET /v1/documents/{id}` returns latest.
- `GET /v1/documents/{id}/versions` lists all with timestamps & created_by.
- `POST /v1/documents/{id}/restore?version=N` atomically restores + creates new version (audit trail).

**Response headers:**
```
X-Version: 3
X-Created-At: 2026-10-12T14:32:00Z
X-Created-By: user_id
```

**Decisions:**
- No header versioning (`If-Match` ETags): complex for documents that change (requires every client to track hashes). Simpler to just version all writes.
- Version is integer, auto-increment (immutable, fast index).
- No branching/tags—straight line of versions. Branch complexity ≠ return on investment for most doc stores.
- Restore creates new version (not "roll back in place"). Preserves audit chain; someone can always see "I restored v3".

---

## Error Format

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_INPUT",
    "message": "Document title is required",
    "status": 400,
    "timestamp": "2026-10-12T14:32:00Z",
    "request_id": "req_abc123",
    "details": {
      "field": "title",
      "constraint": "required"
    }
  }
}
```

**Common codes:**
- `400`: `INVALID_INPUT`, `INVALID_PAGINATION`
- `401`: `UNAUTHORIZED`
- `403`: `FORBIDDEN` (wrong tenant, no permission)
- `404`: `NOT_FOUND`
- `409`: `CONFLICT` (version mismatch on concurrent write, if you add optimistic locking)
- `429`: `RATE_LIMITED`
- `500`: `INTERNAL_ERROR`

**Decisions:**
- One error object, not array (simpler, covers 99% of cases).
- `code` (machine-readable) + `message` (human-readable). Skip custom error subfields if they're not really different.
- `request_id` for tracing (log it server-side, user can report it).
- No error `id` field—that's what `code` is for.
- No stack traces in production (ever).

---

## Summary of Trade-offs

| Choice | Why | Cost |
|--------|-----|------|
| Tenant in JWT, not URL | No routing mistakes, cleaner middleware | Can't easily switch tenants mid-request (good) |
| Offset/limit pagination | Simple, works for small→medium datasets | Slow on 100k+ docs (migrate to cursor then) |
| Implicit versions on PUT | No extra endpoint, audit-by-default | Requires version on every update (fine) |
| Soft delete only | Compliance + audit trail | Storage cost (negligible vs. regulatory risk) |
| No ACLs by default | YAGNI—most tenants don't need it | Add per-document perms in DB when asked |
| Bearer JWT, no API keys | Standard, stateless, cacheable | Service-to-service needs separate flows (add if needed) |

**Ship this, add:**
- Search (`/v1/search`) when you have enough docs.
- Concurrent-write conflict detection (`409` on stale PUT) if multiple users edit same doc.
- ACLs if a tenant asks for per-document sharing.
- Cursor pagination if you hit offset performance wall.
